subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native OpenClaw trust/provenance model should govern durable memory writes and retrieval across memory-core, QMD, session memory, Memory Wiki, and plugin/MCP boundaries?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but implementation requires maintainer choices about non-forgeable trust assignment, durable schema and migrations, public config/API shape, retrieval policy, and the boundary between native memory and external MCP/plugin integrations.

options.title: Design Native Trust Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the native security/product tracker and define host-authored trust metadata plus retrieval policy before implementation.

options.title: Split Provenance Foundations First
options.body: Make a durable provenance contract canonical first, then keep this issue for the trust-policy layer that depends on it.

options.title: Rely On External MCP
options.body: Treat world-model-mcp and similar integrations as optional self-serve paths while leaving native OpenClaw memory without trust policy for now.

recommendation.title: Design Native Trust Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the native security/product tracker and define host-authored trust metadata plus retrieval policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has prior review context on this issue and recent history on the memory host/plugin boundaries that need product and security direction.
